applies_why: This judge text decides a pressed link by comparing individual verse bounds, a Matthew application, and an almah/bethulah word-count, so it is doing the chain-collision task K-C governs.
quote: the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8)
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'never verse by verse': one reading bars resolving the collision by individual verse comparisons or word-counts; the other permits noting individual verses only if the final collision is weighed chain against chain by footing. The judge text does the former, not the latter.
why: The judge text leaves D5 vs C5 underdetermined by treating the sign's chapter bounds, Matthew 1:23's application, and the almah/bethulah word-count as separate verse-level points, rather than weighing the pressed chains against each other by footing as K-C requires.
